analysis: Reviewed the docs-only changes. docs/developer/test.md head lines 729-739 add a description of threat-review scanner test coverage: workload segmentation, a 500-request adapter stop, single-attempt transport, no paid work on manual GitHub job reruns, bounded runtime configuration, human review for incomplete outcomes, manual dispatch limited to an unpaid preflight, and a scanner deadline below the job timeout. The rest of test.md (provider tests, endpoint resumption/logout, App Attest dispatch, SSD test volume, cache qualification) is unchanged context. It describes tests and does not alter code or security controls. docs/developer/threat-model-review.md was supplied only as metadata and a truncated patch excerpt, with no head text. The visible hunks narrow the paid-scan trigger: manual dispatch is preflight only, there are no manual depth requests, and each automatic CI review either completes or requires human review. This reduces spend and abuse surface and does not weaken the PR-base immutable threat-model fetch or the rule that PR head code is never checked out. No runtime provider, coordinator, attestation, encryption, cache (T-041), or authorization behavior changed, so no threat-model IDs are implicated. Limitation: the rest of the threat-model-review.md diff (hunks at head 140-164, 324-349, 431-433) was not visible. Whether those changes affect merge-gate clearance semantics, and whether the workflow YAML matches the documented manual-dispatch restriction, belongs to a pass that sees the workflow and scanner code. This is a verification gap, not a finding.
